name: Methandienone

card.summary: The classic oral bulking steroid (Dianabol): small controlled trials show lean-mass gain, with liver, blood-pressure and hormonal costs.
card.note: 17-alpha-alkylated oral steroid with documented liver, blood-pressure and hormonal effects; controlled in many jurisdictions and prohibited in sport.

quick.overview:
Methandienone, sold historically as Dianabol, is an oral anabolic-androgenic steroid taken by strength athletes and bodybuilders to gain muscle mass. On looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums it is described as the traditional first-choice oral for rapid size gains.

A handful of double-blind crossover trials from the 1970s and early 1980s, mostly in trained men on a high dose, found increases in body weight, lean mass, body potassium and nitrogen. Strength gains were significant in some of these trials and not in others, and some researchers noted that part of the weight gain could be water.
quick.mechanism: Methandienone is a synthetic derivative of testosterone that activates the androgen receptor. Trials in trained men reported weight gain confined to the lean part of the body, increases in muscle size and rises in total body potassium and nitrogen, alongside higher cortisol and lower plasma testosterone during use [1][2].
quick.risks: Controlled trials and case reports document water retention, raised systolic blood pressure, side effects leading to withdrawal, suppression of natural testosterone and, in a published case, severe cholestatic liver injury with kidney failure in a bodybuilder also using another steroid [3][4][1]. It is a prohibited substance in sport and is legally restricted in many countries.

lead: Methandienone (also spelled metandienone or methandrostenolone, and sold as Dianabol or D-bol) is a synthetic oral anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from testosterone. It was one of the first anabolic steroids widely used by athletes and remains among the best-known in bodybuilding culture, where it is regarded as a traditional oral compound for gaining mass [1][5][6].

Its effects on body composition were studied in several small controlled trials. In double-blind crossover experiments in athletic men given a high daily dose for six weeks, researchers observed weight gain restricted to lean tissue, larger muscle dimensions and increases in body potassium and nitrogen, while strength gains were not always significantly greater than with placebo [1][2]. A separate crossover trial in weightlifters found greater improvement on the drug than on placebo, together with water retention, a rise in systolic blood pressure and side effects that led three participants to withdraw [7].

Documented harms include cholestatic liver injury, a possible association with pancreatitis, and suppression of the body's own testosterone production [3][4][1]. Within looksmaxxing communities it is mostly discussed as a bulking agent rather than a facial or aesthetic compound; on T Nation it appears in cycle discussions and historical retrospectives.

paras: Methandienone is used non-medically to increase muscle mass and body weight in bodybuilders and strength athletes. Forum members describe it as the oral that produces the fastest visible size gains in a short span, typically stacked with injectable testosterone [8][9][10]. A T Nation poster summarising its history wrote that in the 1970s it was widely regarded as the single best anabolic steroid available [10].

Clinical studies in the mid-twentieth century explored methandienone as an anabolic agent in underweight healthy subjects, in diabetic retinopathy and in psoriasis, and measured its effect on fibrinolytic activity in men with ischaemic heart disease [11][12][13][14]. It was a mainstream pharmaceutical product before its association with athletics; the Dianabol brand was made by CIBA [15].

Human studies of methandienone are mostly small crossover trials: an 11-man double-blind trial (1976), a 7-man repeat with nitrogen measurements (1981), a 13-man weightlifter trial (1975) and a trial in highly trained athletes (1975), all reporting weight or lean-mass gain with variable strength results and side effects including raised blood pressure.[1][2][7][15] Older clinical trials studied it in underweight subjects, diabetic retinopathy, psoriasis and fibrinolysis in ischaemic heart disease.[13][12][14][11]

A 1976 double-blind crossover trial in 11 athletic men on weight training gave a high daily dose for six weeks. Compared with placebo, participants gained about 3.3 kg, accumulated a disproportionately large amount of potassium, and gained lean tissue with larger muscles, but strength and performance did not improve significantly more than on placebo. The authors noted the weight gain might reflect intracellular fluid and said the question of true anabolic action remained open [1].

A 1981 repeat trial in seven male weightlifters, which added measurements of total body nitrogen, reported significant increases in body weight, potassium, nitrogen, muscle size, leg performance and strength on the drug but not on placebo. The authors concluded that the nitrogen and potassium increases were too large to be explained by fluid alone [2].

A 1975 crossover trial in 13 experienced weightlifters on high-protein diets found significantly greater improvement on methandienone (10 or 25 mg a day) than on placebo, with body weight rising in association with water retention [7]. A further double-blind crossover trial in highly trained athletes at moderate dosage was published the same year [15]. Forum members on T Nation sometimes cite the 1976 trial, noting that the published human literature on the compound is sparse [16][17].

Limitations of this literature include very small samples, short durations, high doses and the age of the studies; no large modern randomised trial of methandienone for physique outcomes has been published.

In the 1975 weightlifter trial, methandienone produced many side effects, and three participants withdrew; systolic blood pressure rose significantly [7]. In the 1976 trial, plasma testosterone fell and cortisol rose during treatment [1].

A 1999 case report described a 28-year-old bodybuilder who developed severe cholestasis and acute renal failure after about 80 days of oral methandienone together with injected stanozolol; bilirubin peaked at very high levels and the biochemical values normalised over several weeks after treatment with ursodeoxycholic acid [4]. A 1988 review of drug-induced pancreatitis listed methandienone among drugs with suggestive, but less convincing, evidence of an association, and described pancreatitis as a very rare complication in general [3].

Forensic literature has examined sudden or unnatural deaths among anabolic steroid users, in which multiple substances are commonly involved [18]. A T Nation forum post cited a study of anabolic steroid findings in a Swedish forensic series in which methandienone metabolites were detected in a fifth of cases [19].

Methandienone is a 17-alpha-alkylated derivative of testosterone, a modification that allows oral use. Like other anabolic-androgenic steroids it is understood to act through the androgen receptor; Crossover trials found that it increased total body potassium and nitrogen alongside muscle size [2]. It also altered endocrine function, lowering plasma testosterone and raising cortisol [1].

The metabolites of methandienone have been characterised for anti-doping purposes using mass spectrometry in human, equine and camel liver systems and in a mouse model with a humanised liver [20][21][22][23]. Methandienone has also been detected as an adulterant in dietary supplements, for which immunoassay screening methods have been developed [24].

Surveys of anabolic steroid use by competitive bodybuilders in the late 1980s documented widespread use among them [5]. A Swedish national anti-doping telephone hotline set up in 1993 was developed to capture abuse of doping agents in the general population, and Swedish police case series have recorded anabolic steroid seizures [25][26].

Forum culture around the compound is largely bodybuilding-oriented. T Nation threads mention it in cycle logs, stack discussions with testosterone enanthate and Proviron, and humorous remarks comparing it to other sources of gains [8][27][9]. One poster asked how much muscle from low-dose use persisted after stopping [28]. In a thread about a coaching programme, a poster joked that the product kit contained methandienone [29].

timeline.event: A clinical trial reports methandienone as an anabolic agent in underweight healthy subjects.[13]
A controlled trial tests methandienone in diabetic retinopathy.[12]
Double-blind crossover trials in weightlifters and trained athletes are published, reporting weight gain, water retention and raised blood pressure.[7][15]
A double-blind crossover trial in athletic men finds lean-mass gain but no significantly greater strength gain than placebo.[1]
A repeat trial including body nitrogen measurements reports significant gains in strength and muscle size.[2]
A case report links methandienone and stanozolol use to severe cholestasis with renal failure in a bodybuilder.[4]

lore.intro: On T Nation and related bodybuilding forums, methandienone is discussed as the archetypal oral bulking steroid and a historical reference point for mass gains; its appearance in looksmaxxing spaces is mainly as a size compound rather than a facial one.[10][27]

claims.claim: Dianabol is the classic fast mass builder.
claims.believers: Forum posters say it was widely accepted in the 1970s as the single best anabolic steroid and that the only variable was dose, and that users see rapid size gains in a short period.[10]
claims.experts: Crossover trials in trained men reported weight gain in the lean compartment, with increases in potassium, nitrogen and muscle size, though one trial found strength gains no greater than placebo and noted possible fluid contribution.[1][2]

claims.claim: Gains from methandienone are largely water.
claims.believers: Some forum users argue its size effects are mostly fluid retention and are lost after stopping, and ask how much persists after cessation.[28]
claims.experts: The 1976 authors left open whether weight gain reflected intracellular fluid, while the 1981 repeat trial found nitrogen increases too large to be explained by fluid alone; the 1975 weightlifter trial associated weight gain with water retention.[1][2][7]

claims.claim: Published human research on the compound is scarce, so anecdote dominates.
claims.believers: T Nation posters point to a single 1976 study when arguing that the claimed effects of steroids on bodybuilders are poorly documented.[16][17]
claims.experts: At least four small controlled trials from 1975 to 1981 exist, along with older clinical studies, but none is large or recent.[1][2][15][7]

claims.claim: Oral steroids can be run alongside injectables with support drugs to limit side effects.
claims.believers: Users post cycle plans combining methandienone with testosterone and ancillary medications, saying they manage side effects such as gynecomastia.[8][9]
claims.experts: Clinical literature documents blood-pressure elevation, hormonal suppression and a case of severe cholestasis with kidney failure; no trial has tested ancillary-drug strategies for methandienone.[7][1][4]
